John von Neumann was a mathematician, born in 1903 in Budapest, who did basic work in mathematics, quantum mechanics, game theory and the design of computers.

He was one of a group of brilliant Hungarian Jewish scientists, with Leo Szilard, Eugene Wigner and Edward Teller, who left Europe for the United States. At Princeton from 1930, he wrote the mathematical basis of quantum mechanics and, with Oskar Morgenstern, founded game theory in 1944. He worked on the Manhattan Project. His 1945 report on the EDVAC described the stored program design, where a computer keeps its program in memory with its data, still the basis of most computers. He died of cancer in 1957.
